title: Audit Readiness Checklist: How to Prepare for a Financial Audit
summary: A complete audit readiness checklist by phase: close the books, reconcile accounts, gather support, document controls, and prepare the PBC list, plus how to stay audit-ready.
body_markdown:
An audit does not have to be a fire drill. Most of the stress, the late nights pulling support, the balances no one can explain, the controls nobody documented, comes from treating audit prep as an event instead of a state. An **audit readiness checklist** turns it into a process: a clear list of what has to be true for your books, your support, and your controls before the auditors arrive.


This guide is a complete audit readiness checklist, organized by phase, plus what auditors most often flag and how to stay audit-ready year-round instead of scrambling at year-end.


## **What is audit readiness?**


Audit readiness is the state of having your financial records, supporting documentation, and internal controls complete, reconciled, and traceable, so an external auditor can verify them with minimal back-and-forth. A team is audit-ready when every material balance ties to support, every control is documented and operating, and any number can be traced back to its source.


> Audit readiness is not something you do the month before the audit. It is a property of how you close every month: if each period ends reconciled, documented, and traceable, the audit is a review, not a reconstruction.


## **The audit readiness checklist**


Work through these phases in order. Each builds on the last, and the gaps auditors find usually trace back to skipping one.


### **Phase 1: Close the books**


- All sub-ledgers closed and posted to the general ledger.
- Period cutoff applied correctly, revenue, expenses, and accruals in the right period.
- Trial balance finalized and tied to the GL.
- Intercompany transactions matched and eliminated.


### **Phase 2: Reconcile every account**


- Every balance-sheet account reconciled to support. See[balance sheet reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/balance-sheet-reconciliation) .
- Bank and cash accounts reconciled. See[account reconciliation automation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/account-reconciliation-automation) .
- Fixed asset, prepaid, accrual, and debt roll-forwards complete.
- Reconciling items identified, explained, and cleared, not carried forward unexplained.


### **Phase 3: Gather documentation and support**


- Every material balance tied to source documentation.
- Invoices, contracts, bank statements, and confirmations on file and current.
- Support organized and retrievable, not scattered across inboxes and drives.
- A clear audit trail from each number back to the source records behind it.


### **Phase 4: Document internal controls**


- Key controls documented and operating over the period.
- Segregation of duties in place and evidenced.
- Approvals and sign-offs captured for material transactions. See[SOX compliance software](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/sox-compliance-software) and[continuous controls monitoring](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/continuous-controls-monitoring) .
- Control exceptions logged and remediated.


### **Phase 5: Prepare the PBC list**


- Prepared-by-client (PBC) request list reviewed and assigned to owners.
- Schedules and lead sheets prepared for material accounts.
- Prior-year audit adjustments and findings addressed.
- Significant estimates and judgments documented with rationale.


### **Phase 6: Review and sign-off**


- Management review of the financial statements and disclosures.
- Analytical review and[flux](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/what-is-flux-analysis) explanations ready for material variances.
- Open items tracked to closure with a clear owner.
- Audit timeline, scope, and points of contact agreed with the audit team.


## **What auditors most often flag**


When an audit drags, it is usually one of these, and every one is preventable with the checklist above:


- **Unreconciled or unexplained balances.** An account that does not tie to support, or a reconciling item no one can explain.
- **Numbers that cannot be traced.** A balance with no clear path back to source documentation.
- **Weak or undocumented controls.** Controls that exist in practice but were never evidenced.
- **Cutoff errors.** Revenue or expenses booked in the wrong period.
- **Late or disorganized PBC responses.** Requests that take days to fulfill because the support was not ready.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is an audit readiness checklist?**


An audit readiness checklist is a structured list of everything that must be true before a financial audit: the books closed, every account reconciled to support, documentation gathered and traceable, internal controls documented and operating, and the PBC list prepared. It turns audit prep from a scramble into a repeatable process.


### **How do you prepare for a financial audit?**


Close the books with correct cutoff, reconcile every balance-sheet account to support, gather and organize documentation so each number traces to source, document that internal controls operated, prepare the prepared-by-client (PBC) schedules, and complete a management review before the auditors begin.


### **What do auditors ask for?**


Auditors issue a prepared-by-client (PBC) list: reconciliations, schedules and roll-forwards for material accounts, supporting documentation (invoices, contracts, bank statements, confirmations), evidence that controls operated, and documentation of significant estimates and judgments. Having these ready in advance is the core of audit readiness.


### **How do you stay audit-ready year-round?**


Close and reconcile every period on time, attach support as you go, document controls as they operate, and keep an audit trail that ties every number to source, rather than reconstructing it at year-end. Continuous accounting and AI agents that run reconciliations and maintain the audit trail make year-round readiness practical.


## **The bottom line**


An audit readiness checklist, closing the books, reconciling every account, gathering traceable support, documenting controls, and preparing the PBC list, is what turns an audit from a reconstruction into a review. The teams that dread audits least are the ones for whom every one of those is already true before the auditors arrive.
